Once you find a good price on Kayak or Priceline call the actual hotel. Sometimes the hotel will match or go lower than the sites. It won't work if the hotel outsources bookings but a small percent of the time this works.

For hotels, look for rates online (expedia, trivago, priceline, etc.) and the hotel website you want to go to. If the rate is lower on any other places than the hotel's website, call the hotel directly and ask them to pricematch. They will gladly do so and you will have a better service once you're at the hotel (and increase your change of getting an upgrade).

When you book on an other site online, the hotel will take you as a second rate client (especially true with expedia). When they are soldout, the hotel will make less effort to accomodate you and sometimes even downgrade you. When they are soldout, they will always privilege the ones who booked through them first.

You booked the wrong date and you're at the front desk? Just too bad if you didn't booked directly with the hotel. They will tell you they can't do anything and that you need to call the site you booked on.

Source : I work in a hotel.
